newsitem.title: CANADA: Newcourt to put up US$10 mln in Dell deal.
newsitem.headline: Newcourt to put up US$10 mln in Dell deal.

text.p: Newcourt Credit Group Inc and Dell Computer Corp said on Monday that Newcourt would put up US$10 million of working capital for their new joint venture leasing company Dell Financial Services LP, but could earn about US$40 million a year from the deal.

On a media conference call, Newcourt Chief Executive Steven Hudson would not repeat annual meeting forecasts of US$35 to US$40 million of income from the deal, but hinted they might not be far off the mark.

"I would prefer not to comment on forecasts, but I'd like to say that Dell has about US$5 billion in U.S. sales and as Michael (Dell) mentioned, industry experts indicate that capital finance companies like this one enjoy about a 20 percent penetration rate, meaning that out of every 10 sales two will be financed. I'll leave you to do the math."
Dell Chief Executive Michael Dell told the call that industry experts estimated that leasing accounted for about 26 percent of computer revenues.
"In fact this number has been growing as more and more customers understand the benefits of leasing, including technology rotation," Dell said.
Although both executives called the deal "exclusive," neither said the deal would preclude the two companies from doing similar deals with companies in other countries.
Hudson said the deal would not change Newcourt's core strategy in terms of credit risk.
"This is not a change in Newcourt's investment or credit policies," Hudson said, adding that the venture was an equal partnership.

Dell and Newcourt said earlier today that they formed Dell Financial Services LP (DFS) to offer leasing and asset management services to Dell's customers in the United States and eventually worldwide.
